greater-kailash-1.name: Greater Kailash 1
greater-kailash-1.about:
Greater Kailash 1, usually called GK-1, is a plotted colony laid out in the early 1960s on farmland acquired from the villages of Zamrudpur and Devli. Its lettered blocks sit around the well-known M and N Block markets, and most of the original bungalows have been rebuilt as builder floors, so one plot often holds several families on separate storeys. Kailash Colony, East of Kailash, Chittaranjan Park, Kalkaji and Lajpat Nagar all lie next to it, and the Outer Ring Road runs close by.

For metro travel, Kailash Colony station on the Violet Line and Greater Kailash station on the Magenta Line are the usual stops, with a short walk or e-rickshaw for the last leg. Block RWAs keep guards at the entrances, so the family should give the tutor's name to the guard before the first class. Street parking near the markets fills up in the evening, and a tutor on a two-wheeler or on foot will find visits easier. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

greater-kailash-2.name: Greater Kailash 2
greater-kailash-2.about:
Greater Kailash 2 was planned as a companion to GK-1 on a fan-shaped layout of lettered blocks, with the busy M Block market running through the centre and smaller markets serving the E and S blocks. Housing is almost entirely independent houses and builder floors on plotted land, many of them rebuilt as separate floors for different families. Chittaranjan Park, Pamposh Enclave and GK-3 sit alongside, and the Outer Ring Road passes along the colony.

Greater Kailash station on the Magenta Line serves GK-2 directly, and Nehru Place on the Violet Line is another option for tutors coming from the east. Blocks are run by RWAs with guards, so tutors are usually asked to sign in at the gate. Floors in the same building often have separate entrances, which keeps weekday evening classes simple once the family shares the floor number. Traffic on the Outer Ring Road builds in the evening peak, so an early or late slot suits tutors crossing the city. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

defence-colony.name: Defence Colony
defence-colony.about:
Defence Colony was set up in 1960 on the old lands of Kotla Mubarakpur village, when land was allotted to resettle military officers displaced by Partition. It is a plotted colony of five blocks, A to E, where many original houses have become builder floors while some independent homes with gardens remain. The Ring Road forms its southern edge, the Delhi Ring Railway runs along the north, and Lajpat Nagar and South Extension are its immediate neighbours.

Metro access is easy: Lajpat Nagar is an interchange of the Violet and Pink Lines, and South Extension station on the Pink Line is also close. Streets are broad and the parks well kept, but parking around the colony market fills up in the evening. Guards at the block entrances keep registers, so families should tell them when a new tutor is expected. Morning and weekend slots are the easiest for tutors driving in along the Ring Road. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

lajpat-nagar.name: Lajpat Nagar
lajpat-nagar.about:
Lajpat Nagar was built in the 1950s to settle families displaced by Partition and is divided into four parts: I, II and III lie north of the Ring Road and IV lies to the south. Homes are mostly independent houses and builder floors along plotted lanes, looked after by RWAs, and colonies such as Amar Colony, Dayanand Colony, Nirmal Puri, National Park and Vikram Vihar sit within or beside it. The Central Market, known for garments and textiles, draws large crowds every day.

Lajpat Nagar station is an interchange between the elevated Violet Line and the underground Pink Line, and Moolchand on the Violet Line serves the western side. Because of the market crowds, tutors do better arriving by metro and walking or taking an e-rickshaw to the lane rather than looking for parking near the market in the evening. Morning and weekend classes are calmer across all four parts. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

south-extension.name: South Extension
south-extension.about:
South Extension sits along the Ring Road and is divided into Part I and Part II. It grew from the lands of Kotla Mubarakpur village, and Mughal-era tombs still stand among its houses. Homes are mostly builder floors, with some independent houses and low-rise apartments on the inner lanes, while the Ring Road frontage is one of the city's best-known shopping streets. Defence Colony, Lajpat Nagar and Kotla Mubarakpur lie next to it.

South Extension station on the Pink Line opened in August 2018, and the Lajpat Nagar interchange nearby adds the Violet Line. Evening traffic on the Ring Road outside the markets is slow, so tutors travelling by road should plan around the peak or use the metro instead. The inner lanes are residential and quiet, and most floors have their own entrance and bell, which makes regular home classes straightforward once the family shares the floor details. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

east-of-kailash.name: East of Kailash
east-of-kailash.about:
East of Kailash is a mixed-housing colony where independent houses, builder floors, DDA flats and cooperative group housing (CGHS) apartments stand side by side. It borders Kailash Colony, Kailash Hills, Greater Kailash and Lajpat Nagar, and the Nehru Place business district is close by. Because of this mix, one street may have private floors while the next holds a DDA pocket with its own gate and RWA.

The nearest metro stops are Kailash Colony and Nehru Place on the Violet Line, and Kalkaji Mandir, where the Violet and Magenta Lines meet. From these stations an auto or e-rickshaw covers the last leg. In DDA pockets and CGHS societies a tutor's name usually goes into the gate register, while independent floors are simple doorstep visits. Weekday evenings near Nehru Place are busy, so tutors should allow for that when fixing a slot. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

pamposh-enclave.name: Pamposh Enclave
pamposh-enclave.about:
Pamposh Enclave is a small residential colony in the Greater Kailash area with long links to Kashmiri Pandit families; its name comes from the Kashmiri word for the lotus of the Dal Lake. Homes are independent houses and builder floors along wide internal roads, and three playgrounds and two local temples give it a quiet, green feel. It borders Nehru Place, Chirag Enclave, Hemkunt Colony, Greater Kailash Enclave 1, Chittaranjan Park and Kalkaji.

Greater Kailash station on the Magenta Line serves the colony, and Nehru Place on the Violet Line is another option for tutors coming from the east. The roads around the colony are crowded on weekday evenings because of the nearby office district, while the internal lanes stay calm. Families usually inform the colony guard in advance, and parking inside is manageable for a tutor on a two-wheeler. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

saket.name: Saket
saket.about:
Saket was developed by the DDA on the lands of Khirki, Said-ul-Ajaib and Hauz Rani villages and is organised into lettered residential blocks from A to N, plus a Press Enclave. The blocks mix row houses, low-rise DDA flats and multi-storey apartments. Malviya Nagar and Geetanjali Enclave lie to the north, Pushp Vihar to the east, Mehrauli to the west and Sainik Farm to the south, and the district centre with offices, courts and large shopping centres makes the area mixed.

Two underground Yellow Line stations serve it: Saket, on Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, and Malviya Nagar, which is closer to several of the lower-lettered blocks. DDA blocks usually have gate guards who note visitors, and inner parking is limited, so tutors often come by metro and take an e-rickshaw. Traffic near the district centre is heavy on weekend evenings, which makes weekday or morning slots easier. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

malviya-nagar.name: Malviya Nagar
malviya-nagar.about:
Malviya Nagar grew in the 1950s on part of Shahpur Jat village land as a settlement for families displaced by Partition. Today it is a large residential area of independent houses, builder floors and DDA flats, taking in sub-localities such as Geetanjali Enclave, Navjeevan Vihar, Shivalik, Begumpur, Sarvodaya Enclave and MMTC Colony. Panchsheel Enclave lies to the north, Sheikh Sarai to the east, Saket to the south and Hauz Khas to the west, with the Outer Ring Road along one side.

Malviya Nagar station on the Yellow Line is the main metro stop, and Hauz Khas, one stop north, links to the Magenta Line. Lanes in the older blocks are narrow and parking is tight, so a two-wheeler or an e-rickshaw from the station works best. Plotted blocks have RWA guards, and families generally let them know before a tutor's first visit. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

hauz-khas.name: Hauz Khas
hauz-khas.about:
Hauz Khas Enclave was developed in the 1960s by a private developer as a plotted colony of blocks lettered A to Z, around the medieval Hauz Khas tank and the older Hauz Khas Village. The E Block market, with its multi-level parking, is the local shopping centre. Green Park lies to the west, Gulmohar Park to the north, Sarvapriya Vihar and the Outer Ring Road to the south and the Asiad Village and Siri Fort side to the east, with Safdarjung Enclave and Padmini Enclave also close.

Hauz Khas station is an interchange between the Yellow Line and the Magenta Line, and Green Park on the Yellow Line serves the northern blocks. Blocks have RWA guards, so families should share a tutor's name before the first class. Hauz Khas Village draws crowds in the evenings and at weekends, so tutors driving in should avoid the village approach roads at those times and use the metro where possible. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

green-park.name: Green Park
green-park.about:
Green Park was established in the early 1960s and has two parts, Green Park Main and Green Park Extension. Homes range from builder floors to independent houses, and the colony sits among Hauz Khas, Safdarjung Enclave and the Safdarjung Development Area. It is bounded by the Ring Road, the Outer Ring Road and Africa Avenue, with the Deer Park and five protected Lodi-period monuments close by.

Green Park station on the Yellow Line lies at its edge, and the Hauz Khas interchange with the Magenta Line is one stop south. Traffic on the main roads can be heavy at peak hours, so a settled after-school slot helps. Inside the colony the lanes are quiet and most floors have their own entrance, which makes regular evening classes straightforward. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

safdarjung-enclave.name: Safdarjung Enclave
safdarjung-enclave.about:
Safdarjung Enclave was developed in the early 1960s by a private developer on farmland acquired from Humayunpur village, and the Safdarjung Development Area was added later in that decade as an extension to the south. The locality has plotted houses and builder floors alongside DDA and cooperative flats, and takes in Arjun Nagar and the Humayunpur urban village. It lies south of the Ring Road and north of the Deer Park, with Green Park and Hauz Khas as neighbours.

Bhikaji Cama Place on the Pink Line is next to the enclave, Green Park on the Yellow Line is close to the eastern side, and R. K. Puram on the Magenta Line serves the western blocks. The Outer Ring Road gives direct access by car. Blocks have RWA guards, and families in DDA and cooperative flats usually register visitors at the gate, so sharing a tutor's name in advance saves time. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

sheikh-sarai.name: Sheikh Sarai
sheikh-sarai.about:
Sheikh Sarai is a DDA-developed residential area in two phases, Phase 1 and Phase 2, with DDA flats, multi-storey apartment blocks and some independent houses. It lies on the eastern side of Malviya Nagar and is close to Panchsheel Park and Chirag Delhi, sharing the 110017 pin code with its neighbours.

Chirag Delhi station on the Magenta Line is the closest metro stop, and Malviya Nagar on the Yellow Line is another option. Most buildings are DDA-built without basement parking, so cars line the internal roads and spaces fill up in the evening; a tutor coming by metro and e-rickshaw avoids that. Pockets have RWAs and gate guards, so the family should share the tutor's name before the first class. Weekend mornings are usually the calmest time for longer sessions. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

panchsheel-park.name: Panchsheel Park
panchsheel-park.about:
Panchsheel Park is an upscale plotted colony of independent houses and builder floors on large plots, with wide tree-lined streets and the Hauz Khas District Park close by. Hauz Khas lies to the west, Panchsheel Enclave to the east and Malviya Nagar to the south, with Chirag Delhi, Sheikh Sarai and Sarvapriya Vihar also nearby. The Outer Ring Road runs along the colony.

Panchsheel Park station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018 and shares the colony's name, while Hauz Khas, one stop away, links to the Yellow Line. Blocks have guarded entrances and many houses have their own security, so families usually tell the guard when a tutor is expected. Evening traffic on the Outer Ring Road is slow, which makes the metro the easier way in for tutors from other parts of the city. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

sarvodaya-enclave.name: Sarvodaya Enclave
sarvodaya-enclave.about:
Sarvodaya Enclave is an affluent residential colony in the Adhchini area of South Delhi, made up of more than 300 standalone houses, many of them now divided into separate floors. It is counted among the sub-localities of Malviya Nagar and sits close to Hauz Khas. The colony is known for its trees, which residents counted in a tree census in 2012.

Hauz Khas, the interchange of the Yellow and Magenta Lines, is the nearest metro station, and the colony has easy road access towards both Gurugram and Noida. From the station an e-rickshaw covers the last leg. The colony has guarded entrances, and since many houses are split into floors, the family should share the floor and gate details before a tutor's first visit. Evening classes are easy to arrange because the internal roads stay quiet. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

shivalik.name: Shivalik
shivalik.about:
Shivalik, often listed as Shivalik Colony, is a sub-locality of Malviya Nagar made up mostly of independent houses and builder floors, with only a few flats. It sits among Malviya Nagar's other enclaves such as Geetanjali Enclave, Navjeevan Vihar, Begumpur and Sarvodaya Enclave, and the wider area lies between Saket and Hauz Khas, close to the Outer Ring Road.

Malviya Nagar station on the Yellow Line is the usual metro stop, with an e-rickshaw for the last leg, and Hauz Khas adds the Magenta Line. Blocks are managed by RWAs with guards at the gates, so families should tell them when a tutor is due. Parking along the lanes is limited in the evening, so a tutor on a two-wheeler, or one walking from the e-rickshaw stand, will find visits simpler. Floors with separate entrances make regular weekday classes easy to fit in. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

sainik-farm.name: Sainik Farm
sainik-farm.about:
Sainik Farm lies south of Saket, beyond the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road. It began in the 1960s as a cooperative society for defence staff and their families, and today it is known for large independent houses, villas and farmhouse-style homes on big plots, with some builder floors. Neb Sarai and Khanpur are close by, and Chhatarpur and Freedom Fighters Enclave are part of the wider neighbourhood.

The nearest metro stations are Saket and Qutub Minar on the Yellow Line, so a tutor coming by metro will need an auto or cab for the last leg. Houses are spread out along internal roads with private gates and staff, and guards generally check visitors, so families should share the tutor's name and the exact lane before the first visit. Traffic on the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road builds in the evening peak, so tutors should plan their arrival around it. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

chhatarpur.name: Chhatarpur
chhatarpur.about:
Chhatarpur is a large locality on the Mehrauli side of South Delhi, close to the Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road. Housing is varied, from affordable builder floors in Chhatarpur Enclave and the surrounding lanes to large farmhouses and villas, and the area is known for its big temple complex and a farmhouse belt that keeps it greener than most of the city. Mehrauli, Kishangarh, Sainik Farm and Vasant Kunj are close by.

Chhatarpur station on the Yellow Line opened in August 2010 on the Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road, and Qutub Minar station is another option. Lanes in the enclaves are narrow and parking is tight, so e-rickshaws from the station are the usual last leg. Temple crowds on festival days and weekends slow the main road, so weekday slots are easier for visiting tutors. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mehrauli.name: Mehrauli
mehrauli.about:
Mehrauli is one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in Delhi, and its old village core sits beside the Qutub Minar complex and the Mehrauli Archaeological Park. Housing today is mostly builder floors, with some apartments and independent houses, spread across sub-localities such as Seth Sarai and Garhwal Colony. Malviya Nagar lies to the north and Vasant Kunj to the west, with Chhatarpur, Kishangarh and Freedom Fighters Enclave close by.

Qutub Minar station on the Yellow Line is the main metro stop, with Chhatarpur and Saket also within reach, and the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road and Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road are the main routes by car. The older lanes are narrow and parking is scarce, so tutors usually come by metro and e-rickshaw or on a two-wheeler. Families should share a landmark and lane details, as addresses in the old village can be hard to find on a first visit. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

kalkaji.name: Kalkaji
kalkaji.about:
Kalkaji is a large residential area around the historic Kalkaji temple, opposite the Nehru Place business district. Housing is mainly DDA flats, including janta flats, alongside builder floors and independent houses in the plotted blocks. Greater Kailash, Chittaranjan Park, Alaknanda, Nehru Place and Sukhdev Vihar are neighbours, and the Outer Ring Road runs close by.

Metro choice is good: Kalkaji Mandir is an interchange between the Violet Line, open since October 2010, and the Magenta Line, open since December 2017, while Govindpuri on the Violet Line and Nehru Enclave on the Magenta Line serve other blocks. DDA pockets have gates and RWA registers, so the family should give the tutor's name in advance. The temple area gets very crowded during festivals, so plan classes around those days or switch them online. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

chittaranjan-park.name: Chittaranjan Park
chittaranjan-park.about:
Chittaranjan Park, widely called CR Park, began in the early 1960s as the East Pakistan Displaced Persons Colony for Bengali families and was renamed in the 1980s. Homes stand on around 2,000 plots in blocks A to K, with blocks M, N, O, P, K-1 and K-2 added in the 1990s, plus Pocket 40 and Pocket 52. Kalkaji, GK-1 and GK-2, Alaknanda and Govindpuri surround it, and its markets and Durga Puja festivities give it a strong Bengali character.

Greater Kailash and Nehru Enclave stations on the Magenta Line serve the western and southern blocks, and Nehru Place on the Violet Line is near B Block. Block gates have guards who note visitors, so families should share the tutor's name in advance. During Durga Puja the colony draws very large crowds, so families often move classes to mornings or online that week. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

alaknanda.name: Alaknanda
alaknanda.about:
Alaknanda is a planned residential area of DDA and cooperative apartment complexes, many named after rivers and hills, set among parks and green belts that keep the internal lanes quiet. It borders Kalkaji, Chittaranjan Park, Greater Kailash, Nehru Place, Govindpuri and Dakshinpuri, with the Outer Ring Road nearby.

There is no metro station inside Alaknanda; the nearest stops are Nehru Enclave and Greater Kailash on the Magenta Line and Govindpuri on the Violet Line, followed by an auto or e-rickshaw. Each apartment complex has its own gate, guards and visitor register, so the family should tell the gate about a new tutor. Mornings near the local schools are busy on the roads, and parking in the inner lanes is limited, so late afternoon or evening slots are often easier for tutors. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

nehru-enclave.name: Nehru Enclave
nehru-enclave.about:
Nehru Enclave, on the Kalkaji side of the Nehru Place business district, was developed by the DDA in planned sectors of multi-storey apartment complexes with some independent houses. East of Kailash, Kalkaji, Chittaranjan Park, Nehru Place and Bahapur surround it, and the Outer Ring Road passes close by. Many families here live in DDA and cooperative apartment blocks with their own RWAs.

Nehru Enclave station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018 in Kalkaji's Block C, and Nehru Place on the Violet Line is also close. Because the office district is next door, the roads are busy on weekday evenings, so tutors often arrive by metro and walk or take an e-rickshaw. Apartment blocks keep gate registers, so the family should pass on the tutor's name in advance. Weekend classes are easier to reach by car. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

sarita-vihar.name: Sarita Vihar
sarita-vihar.about:
Sarita Vihar was built by the DDA on land from Madanpur Khadar village and was first planned as a village for the 1982 Asian Games before becoming a residential colony. It is organised into lettered pockets of DDA and cooperative flats, each usually with its own RWA, and sits on Mathura Road close to the Uttar Pradesh border. Jasola, Madanpur Khadar and Mohan Estate lie nearby, and an underpass opened in 2014 improved the link towards Okhla.

Sarita Vihar station on the Violet Line opened in October 2010 in Pocket C, and Jasola Apollo is one stop north. Pocket gates have guards and visitor registers, so families should share the tutor's name before the first class. Mathura Road carries heavy traffic at peak hours, so tutors driving in should plan around them or use the metro. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

jasola-vihar.name: Jasola Vihar
jasola-vihar.about:
Jasola Vihar is a DDA-planned area of residential pockets with DDA flats and builder floors, set beside a growing office district. Sarita Vihar, Shaheen Bagh, Okhla and Tekhand are its neighbours, with the Yamuna floodplain near Kalindi Kunj to the east, and Mathura Road is the main link road.

Two metro lines serve the area: Jasola Vihar Shaheen Bagh on the Magenta Line, opened in December 2017, and Jasola Apollo on the Violet Line, opened in October 2010. Pockets have RWA gates and visitor parking is limited, so tutors often arrive by metro and walk or take an e-rickshaw. With offices nearby, roads are busiest at office hours, so evening classes after the rush work well. Families should share the pocket number and gate with the tutor before the first visit. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka.name: Dwarka
dwarka.about:
Dwarka is the planned sub-city built by the Delhi Development Authority in South West Delhi, laid out as numbered sectors separated by wide arterial roads. Most families live in cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies and DDA flats, with builder floors in some pockets and older villages along the edges. The Blue Line runs through the middle of the sub-city with stations at Sectors 8 to 14 and at Sector 21, where the Airport Express also stops, before carrying on past Dwarka Mor. On the eastern side the Magenta Line serves Palam and Dashrathpuri.

For a home tutor, the numbered-sector grid makes addresses easy to find, but almost every society has a guard at the gate and a visitor register. Share the tower and flat number, and let the guard know the tutor's name before the first class. Many tutors arrive by metro and cover the last stretch by e-rickshaw, so a fixed weekly slot works better than changing times each week. Families who want a specialist subject tutor often mix home classes with online sessions. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-4.name: Dwarka Sector 4
dwarka-sector-4.about:
Apartments make up almost all the housing in Sector 4, most of them three-bedroom flats in cooperative group housing societies planned by the DDA in the middle of the sub-city. Neighbouring sectors include 3, 5, 11, 12 and 13, so the sector sits among some of Dwarka's older and more settled societies. There is no metro station inside the sector; families usually use the Blue Line stations at Sector 12 and Sector 13.

Because nearly every home is inside a gated society, tutors should expect to sign in at the main gate on each visit, and some societies ask residents to pre-approve regular visitors. A tutor who lives in a nearby sector can often walk or take an e-rickshaw from the metro, which keeps evening classes predictable. Senior-school students who need a specialist for one subject often combine a local home tutor with online classes. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-5.name: Dwarka Sector 5
dwarka-sector-5.about:
Sector 5 is an apartment sector: society flats account for nearly all homes for sale here, with a few builder floors in the rental market. It borders Sectors 4, 6, 10 and 12, and like most of Dwarka it was planned by the DDA around cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies. The closest metro options are the Blue Line stations at Sector 10 and Sector 12, just outside the sector.

For tuition at home, the main practical point is the society gate. Guards usually call the flat or check a visitor list, so it helps to register the tutor as a regular visitor from the first week. Tutors coming by metro generally finish the trip by e-rickshaw or on foot. Weekday evening slots fill up first in family sectors like this one, so book the time early; for board-exam subjects that need a specialist, online classes are a sensible addition. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-6.name: Dwarka Sector 6
dwarka-sector-6.about:
On the eastern side of Dwarka, Sector 6 is made up of multi-storey society apartments and DDA self-financing scheme flats. It touches Sectors 2, 5, 7 and 10, and just beyond it lie the older colonies of Palam Extension, Dabri and Mahavir Enclave. Pankha Road is the main arterial road on this side. The sector has no metro station of its own: residents use the Blue Line stop at Sector 10 and the Magenta Line stop at Palam.

Having two metro lines nearby helps when a tutor is coming from Janakpuri, Palam or other Dwarka sectors. Societies keep guards and gate registers, so give the tutor's name at the gate in advance. Roads towards Pankha Road and the Dabri flyover get busy in the evening, so a class that starts a little before the rush is easier to keep on time. Online classes can cover a specialist subject that no nearby tutor teaches. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-7.name: Dwarka Sector 7
dwarka-sector-7.about:
Families in Sector 7 live mainly in society apartments, with some builder floors and a few shops on the main roads. It is one of the sectors nearest the old Palam side of Dwarka: Sectors 1, 6, 8 and 9 surround it, and Mahavir Enclave and Palam are close by. Residents usually use the Magenta Line station at Palam or the Blue Line station at Sector 10.

Tutors who travel by metro can come in on either line and take an e-rickshaw for the last part of the trip, which gives some flexibility when one route is crowded. Societies here have guarded gates and visitor registers, so let the guard know about a regular tutor. Parking inside societies is usually for residents, so a tutor arriving by car or scooter should check where visitors may park. Online classes suit subjects where a local specialist is hard to find. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-9.name: Dwarka Sector 9
dwarka-sector-9.about:
The Blue Line's Dwarka Sector 9 station, open since April 2006, gives this sector one of the older metro links in the sub-city. Housing is a mix of cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies, DDA flats and some builder floors, spread across several pockets. Sector 10 is next door, and the sector sits on the stretch of the Blue Line that leads towards Sector 21 and the Airport Express.

With a station inside the sector, tutors who come by metro can usually walk to the society gate or take a short e-rickshaw ride. Guards at society gates keep a register, and some ask for a call to the flat before letting a visitor in, so share the pocket, tower and flat number. For older students preparing for board or entrance exams, families often pair a home tutor for the main subject with online classes for the rest. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-10.name: Dwarka Sector 10
dwarka-sector-10.about:
Sector 10 is one of the busier sectors in Dwarka, with its own Blue Line station, a bus terminal and the shops and eateries around Ashirwad Chowk. Homes are mostly society apartments, both low-rise and newer high-rise, with some builder floors. It is surrounded by Sectors 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 19, and Madhu Vihar and Palam Extension lie close by.

Good public transport makes this an easy sector for tutors to reach: many can take the Blue Line straight to Sector 10 and walk to the society. The market area and metro roads get crowded in the evening, so allow for that when fixing class times. Most homes are inside gated societies with a guard and visitor register, so registering a regular tutor once saves time on later visits. Online classes can fill in for specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-11.name: Dwarka Sector 11
dwarka-sector-11.about:
Low-rise and high-rise cooperative housing societies make up most of Sector 11, with some builder floors as well. The sector has its own Blue Line station, which gives a direct ride towards Rajiv Chowk and central Delhi. Around it are Sectors 4, 5, 10, 12, 13 and 18, with Madhu Vihar and Palam Extension a little further away.

A tutor coming from another sector along the Blue Line can reach most societies here by metro and a short walk or e-rickshaw ride. Each society has its own gate rules; most keep a guard register and some pre-approve regular visitors, so sort this out before the first class. Evening traffic around the markets and metro roads is heavier, so a steady slot is easier to keep. Specialist subjects can be covered online when a local tutor is not available. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-12.name: Dwarka Sector 12
dwarka-sector-12.about:
Well-kept DDA flats and cooperative group housing societies line the roads of Sector 12, along with some builder floors. The Dwarka Sector 12 station on the Blue Line is inside the sector, with shopping complexes close to it, and neighbouring Sectors 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14 are all close by. This central position makes it one of the most connected parts of the sub-city.

For families, the metro station means a tutor from almost anywhere along the Blue Line can reach the sector without a car. Most homes are in gated societies with a guard, so share the flat number and ask the guard to note the tutor as a regular visitor. The commercial area near the metro is busy in the evening, which is worth keeping in mind for early-evening classes. Online sessions work well for subjects where the right tutor lives further away. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-13.name: Dwarka Sector 13
dwarka-sector-13.about:
Between Sectors 12 and 14, Sector 13 has its own Blue Line station and a mix of cooperative housing societies and mid-rise DDA flats. Sectors 11, 18 and 19 are also nearby, and Pankha Road runs on this side of Dwarka towards Janakpuri and Uttam Nagar. The Sector 12 and Sector 14 stations are each one stop away.

Tutors who travel by metro find this sector easy to reach, and many societies are within walking distance of the station. Society gates have guards and visitor registers; some want the resident to confirm each visit, so it is worth arranging standing permission for a regular tutor. For board classes, families often book a home tutor for maths or science and use online classes for other subjects or for extra revision. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-14.name: Dwarka Sector 14
dwarka-sector-14.about:
Most homes in Sector 14 are DDA flats, from one to three bedrooms, along with some newer residential projects. It sits at the Kakrola end of the sub-city, with Sectors 13, 16B and 17 as neighbours, and it has its own station on the Blue Line. Beyond it the line carries on to Dwarka and Dwarka Mor.

A station in the sector makes it simple for tutors from other Blue Line sectors, or from Uttam Nagar and Janakpuri, to come by metro. DDA pockets and societies usually have guarded entries, so tell the guard about a regular tutor and share the block and flat number. Sector roads are wide, but the stretch near the metro and bus stand gets busy in the evening, so a fixed class time helps. Online tutors can cover specialist subjects when needed. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-19.name: Dwarka Sector 19
dwarka-sector-19.about:
Planned by the DDA, Sector 19 combines apartment complexes with the older lanes of Ambrahi village, and it has a large district park and a sports complex. Its neighbours are Sectors 10, 11, 12, 18 and 23. There is no metro station inside the sector; the closest are the Blue Line stations at Sector 10 and Sector 12.

Because housing ranges from gated societies to village lanes, the tutor's route depends on the address. Society flats have a guard and a visitor register, while village homes usually open straight onto the lane but may have little room for parking. Tutors coming by metro generally take an e-rickshaw from Sector 10 or Sector 12. Families can mix home classes with online sessions when a specialist is needed for a board or entrance subject. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-22.name: Dwarka Sector 22
dwarka-sector-22.about:
Close to the airport end of Dwarka, Sector 22 was developed by the DDA with higher-income-group apartments of three to five bedrooms, alongside cooperative group housing societies. Sectors 19, 21 and 23 are among its neighbours, with Bharthal and Bijwasan further out. The Dwarka Sector 21 station, served by both the Blue Line and the Airport Express, is the main metro stop, and the Delhi section of the Dwarka Expressway passes through this sector.

For a tutor, the Sector 21 interchange is the easiest way in, followed by an e-rickshaw or a walk to the society. Gated societies here keep a guard and visitor register, so the tutor's name should be shared before the first class. Roads leading to the expressway and the airport can be heavy at office hours, so evening classes set a little after the rush tend to run smoothly. Online classes are useful for specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dwarka-sector-23.name: Dwarka Sector 23
dwarka-sector-23.about:
Sector 23 lies in the southern part of Dwarka, towards the airport, with neighbours including Sectors 20 and 22, Pochanpur and Bharthal. Most homes are three-bedroom flats in societies, with some builder floors. The nearest metro options are the Blue Line stations at Sector 21 and Sector 8, and the Airport Express station at Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector 25 is also within reach.

Tutors usually arrive by metro and complete the trip by e-rickshaw, or come by scooter from nearby sectors. Society gates keep a visitor register, and some ask the resident to confirm each visitor, so arrange standing permission for a regular tutor. Village-side lanes near Pochanpur are narrower, which matters for anyone coming by car. Online classes are a practical option for specialist subjects or late-evening revision. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

vasant-kunj.name: Vasant Kunj
vasant-kunj.about:
Vasant Kunj is a large South Delhi colony divided into lettered sectors, each split into pockets and blocks, with DDA flats, builder floors and newer apartment towers. Nelson Mandela Marg runs through it, and it sits on the South-Central Ridge, with Sanjay Van forest nearby and the Jawaharlal Nehru University campus on its north-eastern side. Mahipalpur, Chattarpur, Ber Sarai and Vasant Vihar are nearby, and the closest metro station is Vasant Vihar on the Magenta Line.

Because the metro is not inside the colony, most tutors come by car, scooter or bus, or take the Magenta Line and then an auto. Many pockets are gated with guards who note visitors, so share the sector, pocket and flat number clearly. Nelson Mandela Marg is busy at office hours, so late-afternoon or weekend slots are often easier. Families who need a specialist subject tutor often combine home classes with online sessions. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

vasant-vihar.name: Vasant Vihar
vasant-vihar.about:
Vasant Vihar grew out of a government servants' house-building society formed in 1959, as a planned colony of bungalows and independent houses, and today it also has many builder floors. It has six blocks, A to F, each with a local market, and its main streets are Munirka Marg, Vasant Marg, Poorvi Marg and Paschimi Marg. More than fifty diplomatic missions are located here, and the colony lies close to Chanakyapuri and Munirka. The Vasant Vihar station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018.

Homes open onto quiet residential streets, so tutors usually go straight to the door, although block gates and private security are common. Tell the guard or staff at the house about a regular tutor. A tutor can come by metro and walk or take an auto from the station. Online sessions help when a family wants a specialist for IB, IGCSE or other international programmes. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

munirka.name: Munirka
munirka.about:
Munirka combines an old urban village, urbanised by a notification in March 1954, with a well-known DDA colony of four-storey walk-up flats built in 1975. The Jawaharlal Nehru University campus is to the south and Vasant Vihar to the north-west, while the Outer Ring Road runs past the DDA flats. Munirka station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018 and sits next to R K Puram station.

The two parts are very different for a tutor. DDA flats are reached by stairs in walk-up blocks, usually without a gated society. The village has narrow lanes where parking is hard, so metro or two-wheeler is the practical choice. Traffic on the Outer Ring Road is heavy at office hours, so evening or weekend slots are easier to keep. Online classes fill gaps for specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

r-k-puram.name: R K Puram
r-k-puram.about:
Rama Krishna Puram was built from the late 1950s by the Central Public Works Department as an extension of New Delhi, mainly as double-storey housing blocks for central government officers. Its sectors have local markets in each pocket, and the colony also has cooperative societies and government offices. The R K Puram station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018, with Munirka and IIT stations on either side.

Many families here live in government quarters, where entry is usually open but some blocks have guards at the gate. Tutors coming by metro can walk or take an auto from R K Puram or Munirka station. Roads on the Outer Ring Road side are busy at office hours, so plan evening classes a little after the rush. For senior students, a home tutor for the main subject can be combined with online classes. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

palam.name: Palam
palam.about:
Palam is an old village area in South West Delhi that has grown into a dense residential zone between Delhi Cantonment, Dwarka and Janakpuri. Around it are Palam Colony, Raj Nagar, Mahavir Enclave and Mangla Puri, mostly independent houses and builder floors, and the area has many busy local markets. Palam station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018, and Palam railway station is on the line to Rewari.

Most homes are independent houses or floors, so a tutor usually goes straight to the door rather than through a society gate. Lanes are narrow in places and parking can be hard, so metro, e-rickshaw or two-wheeler is the practical way in. Market roads are crowded in the evening, so it helps to fix a class time before or after the busiest hours. Online classes cover specialist subjects when needed. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mahavir-enclave.name: Mahavir Enclave
mahavir-enclave.about:
Mahavir Enclave is a settled colony in South West Delhi, split into Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3, with independent houses, builder floors and some low-rise flats. Palam-Dabri Marg is the main road, linking it to Dwarka, Janakpuri and Uttam Nagar, and it borders Palam Colony, Dashrathpuri, Manglapuri and Sector 6 of Dwarka. Dashrathpuri station on the Magenta Line is the closest metro, with Palam station also nearby.

Most homes open straight onto the lane, so tutors go to the door without a society gate to pass. Streets are narrow and parking is limited, so metro and e-rickshaw or a two-wheeler is usually easier than a car. Palam-Dabri Marg gets crowded at office hours, so classes set a little away from peak time run more smoothly. Online classes help with specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dabri.name: Dabri
dabri.about:
Dabri began as a village and is now fully urbanised, its farmland having been acquired for the Dwarka and Janakpuri development projects. It is made up of colonies such as Dabri Extension Main, Dabri Extension East, Raghu Nagar, Sitapuri and Syndicate Enclave, mostly builder floors and independent houses. Janakpuri, Palam, Uttam Nagar and Dwarka are close by, and Dabri Mor - Janakpuri South station on the Magenta Line opened in May 2018.

Most homes are floors in plotted lanes, so tutors go straight to the door and meet the family without a society gate. Lanes can be narrow, so metro plus e-rickshaw or a two-wheeler works better than a car. Dabri Mor and Pankha Road are busy at office hours, so plan class times around them. Families can use online tutors for specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

sagarpur.name: Sagarpur
sagarpur.about:
Sagarpur, including West Sagarpur, is a dense residential locality in South West Delhi made up mostly of builder floors and independent houses, with some small apartment buildings. Janakpuri, Palam, Mahavir Enclave, Sitapuri and Vijay Enclave are around it, and Pankha Road runs along one side. The nearest metro stations are Dashrathpuri, Dabri Mor - Janakpuri South and Palam, all on the Magenta Line.

Homes here are in plotted lanes rather than gated societies, so a tutor usually goes directly to the door. Lanes are narrow and parking is scarce, so tutors tend to come by metro and e-rickshaw or on a two-wheeler. Local market roads are busy in the evening, so an early-evening or weekend slot is easier to keep. Online classes suit subjects where a nearby specialist is hard to find. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

janakpuri.name: Janakpuri
janakpuri.about:
Janakpuri was planned in the late 1960s on acquired land and is often described as one of the largest residential colonies in Asia. It is laid out in lettered blocks and pockets, most with their own parks, and homes range from flats in housing societies to houses and floors in the plotted blocks. The Janakpuri District Centre is its main office and shopping hub. Three metro stations serve it: Janakpuri East on the Blue Line, Janakpuri West, which is the Blue and Magenta Line interchange, and Dabri Mor-Janakpuri South on the Magenta Line.

Clear block and pocket numbering makes a first visit easy to find. Tutors arriving by metro usually finish the trip by e-rickshaw from the nearest of the three stations. Society flats tend to ask visitors to sign a guard register, while houses and builder floors are simple doorstep visits. Tutors driving in from Vikaspuri, Uttam Nagar or Paschim Vihar often use the Outer Ring Road, which is slow in the evening peak, so a fixed early-evening slot is easier to keep. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

vikaspuri.name: Vikaspuri
vikaspuri.about:
Vikaspuri is an established residential colony in West Delhi, organised into lettered blocks and sitting along the Outer Ring Road and Najafgarh Road. Builder floors make up most of the housing, alongside DDA flats and a smaller number of independent houses, and M Block Market is the busiest local shopping street. Neighbours include Janakpuri, Tilak Nagar, Hastsal and Uttam Nagar, and the colony has its own district park.

There is no metro station inside the colony itself, so tutors coming by metro generally use the Blue Line stations along Najafgarh Road or Krishna Park Extension on the Magenta Line, then take an e-rickshaw or walk the last stretch. DDA flat blocks may have a guard who notes visitors, while builder floors are usually straight doorstep visits, although street parking can be tight in the inner lanes. The Outer Ring Road between Vikaspuri and Peeragarhi is known for heavy traffic, so tutors who drive plan around the evening rush. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

uttam-nagar.name: Uttam Nagar
uttam-nagar.about:
Uttam Nagar is a large suburb along Najafgarh Road in West Delhi, developed on the lands of Hastsal village and split into Uttam Nagar East and Uttam Nagar West. Most homes are builder floors and privately built houses, and the area grew quickly after the metro arrived. Four Blue Line stations serve it: Uttam Nagar East, Uttam Nagar West, Nawada and Dwarka Mor. Busy local markets run along Hastsal Road, Arya Samaj Road and Bindapur Road, and Janakpuri and Vikaspuri lie next door.

For tutors, the metro is the easiest way in, with e-rickshaws on fixed routes covering the last leg into the lanes. Most visits are to the door of a house or floor rather than through a society gate, so it helps to share a clear landmark and the floor number. Lanes near the markets can be crowded and parking is limited, so tutors driving along Najafgarh Road often prefer weekend or early-evening slots. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

tilak-nagar.name: Tilak Nagar
tilak-nagar.about:
Tilak Nagar grew up on the land of the old Chaukhandi village after Partition, when families from Rawalpindi, Peshawar and other parts of West Punjab settled here. Today it is both a residential area and a busy commercial hub, with markets for clothing, wedding items, timber and hardware. It sits beside Janakpuri, Ashok Nagar, Chand Nagar, Fateh Nagar and Vishnu Garden. Tilak Nagar station on the Blue Line opened on 31 December 2005, and Jail Road and the Outer Ring Road also link the area.

Homes here are a mix of DDA flats, older builder floors and independent houses, so most tutor visits are straight to the door. Market lanes get crowded in the evening, and parking close to the main market is hard to find, so tutors who drive often park a little away and walk. The metro plus a short e-rickshaw ride is often simpler, especially for regular weekday sessions after school hours. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

subhash-nagar.name: Subhash Nagar
subhash-nagar.about:
Subhash Nagar is a compact residential colony in West Delhi, bordered by Tagore Garden and Rajouri Garden to the east, Tilak Nagar and Ashok Nagar to the west and Hari Nagar to the south. Its housing is a mix of DDA flats, independent houses and newer four-storey builder floors. Najafgarh Road is its main road, and Subhash Nagar station on the Blue Line sits right on it, with Tagore Garden on the Blue Line and Mayapuri on the Pink Line also close by.

The metro makes tutor travel straightforward, since most blocks are a short walk or e-rickshaw ride from Subhash Nagar station. DDA flat blocks sometimes have a guard at the gate, while builder floors are doorstep visits, so tell the tutor which floor to come to. Najafgarh Road carries heavy traffic in the evening, which matters more for tutors who drive, so metro-friendly slots tend to run more reliably. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

hari-nagar.name: Hari Nagar
hari-nagar.about:
Hari Nagar lies in West Delhi to the south of Subhash Nagar, with Tilak Nagar and Mayapuri close by. The area has both lettered residential blocks with houses and floors and pockets of DDA flats, and it is a familiar, settled neighbourhood for families. Jail Road and Mayapuri Road are the main approaches. There is no station inside the colony, but Subhash Nagar and Tilak Nagar on the Blue Line and Mayapuri on the Pink Line are all nearby.

Tutors coming by metro usually walk or take an e-rickshaw from Subhash Nagar or Mayapuri. The DDA flat pockets can have a guard at the gate who notes visitors, so share the block and flat number in advance, while houses and floors in the blocks are simple doorstep visits. Jail Road is busy in the evening, so tutors driving in from Janakpuri or Rajouri Garden tend to prefer a fixed slot that avoids the worst of the rush. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rajouri-garden.name: Rajouri Garden
rajouri-garden.about:
Rajouri Garden was developed on land from the former Basai Darapur village and took its name from families from Rajouri who settled here after Partition. It combines private bungalows across lettered blocks with DDA apartment pockets, and it is also a major West Delhi shopping area, with the main market and several malls. Rajouri Garden station is an interchange between the Blue Line and the Pink Line, and Tagore Garden on the Blue Line is also nearby. Neighbours include Subhash Nagar, Tagore Garden, Kirti Nagar and Punjabi Bagh.

The interchange station makes this one of the easier West Delhi areas for tutors to reach by metro from many directions. Bungalows and builder floors are usually doorstep visits, while DDA pockets may have a guard at the gate. Roads around the main market and malls are crowded in the evenings and at weekends, so tutors who drive should allow for parking and choose slots away from the busiest shopping hours. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

punjabi-bagh.name: Punjabi Bagh
punjabi-bagh.about:
Punjabi Bagh began as a settlement for refugees from West Punjab on land acquired from Madipur village, and was known as Refugees Colony until it was renamed in 1960. The Ring Road divides it into Punjabi Bagh East and Punjabi Bagh West. It is known for large bungalow plots and kothis, with some apartments as well. Madipur, Shivaji Park and Punjabi Bagh East are on the Green Line, and Punjabi Bagh West is a Green and Pink Line interchange. Neighbours include Paschim Vihar, Moti Nagar, Rajouri Garden and Ashoka Park.

Wide roads and large houses mean most tutor visits are straightforward doorstep arrivals, often with space to park nearby. If your lane has an RWA gate with a guard, let the guard know a tutor is expected. The Ring Road crossing between the two halves gets busy in the evening peak, so it helps to pick a tutor who lives on the same side, or one who comes by the Green or Pink Line. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

paschim-vihar.name: Paschim Vihar
paschim-vihar.about:
Paschim Vihar is a planned residential area in West Delhi, set along Rohtak Road and the Outer Ring Road. Its homes are mainly DDA flats, group housing societies and builder floors in the plotted blocks, and many residents live in gated DDA or cooperative apartment complexes. Paschim Vihar East and Paschim Vihar West stations are on the Green Line, with the Blue Line reachable by changing at Kirti Nagar. Punjabi Bagh lies next door.

For tutors visiting a society flat, the gate normally checks visitors, so giving the guard the tutor's name ahead of the first session saves time. Builder floors in the blocks are doorstep visits. Frequent buses and the Green Line make it easy to come along Rohtak Road, but traffic on the Outer Ring Road and Rohtak Road builds up in the evening, so tutors who drive tend to prefer an earlier slot. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

kirti-nagar.name: Kirti Nagar
kirti-nagar.about:
Kirti Nagar was settled by refugees from Pakistan after Partition, on the lands of the former Basai Darapur village. Alongside its houses, kothis and builder floors, it is known for a very large furniture market with hundreds of showrooms. It lies next to Ramesh Nagar, Mansarovar Garden, Rajouri Garden, Punjabi Bagh and Patel Nagar, between the Ring Road on one side and Patel Road on the other. Kirti Nagar station is an interchange between the Blue Line and the Green Line.

The interchange helps tutors reach the colony from both the Najafgarh Road side and the Rohtak Road side. Most homes are independent houses or floors, so visits are usually at the door. The furniture market brings heavy daytime traffic and loading vehicles, so tutors who drive in should expect slow movement near the market lanes and are better off with evening or weekend slots once shops start closing. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

moti-nagar.name: Moti Nagar
moti-nagar.about:
Moti Nagar was formed between 1948 and 1950 with help from the Delhi Improvement Trust, to rehouse people who had been living as temporary squatters at Jhandewalan, Shadipur and Basai Darapur. It lies off the Ring Road and Najafgarh Road, with Punjabi Bagh to the north, Kirti Nagar to the south and Karampura to the west. Moti Nagar Market is its local hub, a large DDA district park sits nearby, and Moti Nagar station on the Blue Line serves the area.

Houses and builder floors make most tutor visits simple doorstep arrivals, although parking close to the market can be limited. Tutors coming by metro can walk or take an e-rickshaw from Moti Nagar station. Najafgarh Road and the Ring Road carry heavy evening traffic, so families near the main roads often find that a metro-based tutor keeps time more reliably than one who drives. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

naraina-vihar.name: Naraina Vihar
naraina-vihar.about:
Naraina Vihar is a residential neighbourhood made up of DDA flats and private houses, set beside the western stretch of the Ring Road between Dhaula Kuan and Rajouri Garden. The wider Naraina area also includes an industrial area and the older Naraina village, which sit apart from the residential blocks. Neighbours include Inderpuri, Mayapuri, Kirti Nagar and Delhi Cantonment. Naraina Vihar station on the Pink Line opened in March 2018 and is underground.

Tutors can reach most blocks on foot or by e-rickshaw from Naraina Vihar station. DDA flat blocks may have guards who note visitors, while private houses are doorstep visits. Evening congestion on the Ring Road can slow tutors who drive, so regular slots after the office rush tend to work well. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

karol-bagh.name: Karol Bagh
karol-bagh.zone: Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar
karol-bagh.about:
Karol Bagh is one of Central Delhi's busiest market areas, with residential pockets such as the WEA blocks, Beadon Pura, Dev Nagar and Bapa Nagar set among busy streets. Its population grew in the 1920s when villagers were moved here from the site of Connaught Place, and again after Partition, when traders from West Punjab and Sindh arrived. Homes are mostly builder floors, older houses and flats in low-rise blocks. Karol Bagh station on the Blue Line serves it, with Jhandewalan and Rajendra Place close by, and Pusa Road is a main route.

Because the markets on Ajmal Khan Road, Ghaffar Market and nearby streets draw large crowds, parking is scarce and evenings are congested. Tutors usually come by metro and walk to homes in the WEA and nearby blocks, which are doorstep visits to a floor rather than through a society gate. Weekday sessions often work better than weekend ones, when shopping crowds peak. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

old-rajinder-nagar.name: Old Rajinder Nagar
old-rajinder-nagar.zone: Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar
old-rajinder-nagar.about:
Old Rajinder Nagar grew in the 1950s as a Punjabi refugee colony and sits on the Karol Bagh side of Shankar Road, which separates it from New Rajinder Nagar. It is now one of Delhi's main hubs for civil services coaching, with many coaching centres, hostels and libraries alongside family homes. Housing is mostly builder floors, followed by independent houses. Pusa Road and Shankar Road are its main roads, and Karol Bagh and Rajendra Place stations on the Blue Line are both nearby.

The coaching economy means the lanes stay busy with students well into the evening, and parking is tight. Tutors generally arrive by metro and walk, and visits are to the door of a house or floor. Because many floors are let out to students, give the tutor the exact floor and a landmark, and choose a quieter slot if your lane is close to the main coaching stretch. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

new-rajinder-nagar.name: New Rajinder Nagar
new-rajinder-nagar.zone: Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar
new-rajinder-nagar.about:
New Rajinder Nagar lies between Shankar Road and the Central Ridge, with Old Rajinder Nagar on the other side of Shankar Road and Connaught Place close by. Like its older neighbour, it began as a Punjabi refugee colony in the 1950s, and it is known for green, well-planned blocks with several parks, including a large central park. Rajendra Place station on the Blue Line is the nearest metro, with Karol Bagh station also close.

The quieter streets and parks make this a calmer area for home visits than the coaching lanes across Shankar Road. Most homes are houses and floors, so tutors come straight to the door, and street parking is usually easier to find than in Karol Bagh. Tutors using the Blue Line can walk from Rajendra Place, while those driving should allow for evening traffic on Shankar Road and Pusa Road. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

east-patel-nagar.name: East Patel Nagar
east-patel-nagar.zone: Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar
east-patel-nagar.about:
East Patel Nagar is the part of Patel Nagar closest to Rajendra Place, Karol Bagh and Old Rajinder Nagar. Patel Nagar as a whole was developed on land acquired from Shadipur, Khampur and neighbouring villages, and it is divided into East, West and South Patel Nagar. Housing is mainly builder floors on residential plots. Rajendra Place station on the Blue Line is the most convenient for much of East Patel Nagar, with Patel Nagar station serving its western edge.

Being next to Rajendra Place, the area is easy for tutors to reach by metro, and most visits are doorstep calls to a builder floor. Streets towards Rajendra Place get busy at office closing time, so either an early-evening slot before the rush or a later one tends to be smoother for tutors who drive. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

west-patel-nagar.name: West Patel Nagar
west-patel-nagar.zone: Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar
west-patel-nagar.about:
West Patel Nagar covers the western part of the Patel Nagar area. It borders East Patel Nagar to the east, South Patel Nagar and Shadi Khampur to the south, Baljit Nagar to the west, and Baba Farid Puri and Anand Parbat to the north. Homes are mostly builder floors on residential plots, typical of Patel Nagar. Two Blue Line stations, Patel Nagar and Shadipur, serve different parts of the colony. Neighbouring Patel Road links the area towards Kirti Nagar and the Ring Road.

With two metro stations within reach, tutors can usually walk or take an e-rickshaw to the door. Builder floors mean no society gate to clear, but share the floor number and a landmark for the first visit. Patel Road is busy in the evening peak, so tutors who drive may prefer slots that avoid the main office-closing hours. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

lodhi-colony.name: Lodhi Colony
lodhi-colony.about:
Lodhi Colony was built in the 1940s to house government employees and was one of the last residential areas created in the colonial period. It is managed by the New Delhi Municipal Council and consists mainly of government housing blocks, many of whose walls now carry large murals that earned it the name of India's first open-air public art district. It sits by Lodhi Road and Lodhi Gardens, with several local markets. Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on the Violet Line is the nearest metro station, and Jor Bagh on the Yellow Line is also close.

The blocks are open and well signposted, and visits are usually straight to the flat door. Families here are often in government service, so weekday evening or weekend timings are common. Tutors coming by metro can walk from Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium station, and parking inside the colony is generally manageable outside peak hours. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

jangpura.name: Jangpura
jangpura.about:
Jangpura lies along Mathura Road and includes Jangpura A, Jangpura B, Jangpura Extension, Bhogal and Pant Nagar. It was first laid out in the early twentieth century and grew sharply in 1950 and 1951 as Sikh and Hindu families from West Punjab settled here. Builder floors make up most of the housing today, especially in Jangpura Extension, alongside older houses. Jangpura station on the Violet Line opened in October 2010, with Lajpat Nagar and the Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station also close by.

Most homes are builder floors, so tutors come straight to the door, but lanes in Bhogal and the inner blocks are narrow and parking is tight. Tutors using the Violet Line can walk from Jangpura station. Mathura Road carries heavy evening traffic, so for regular sessions families often choose tutors who travel by metro or live nearby in Lajpat Nagar. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

nizamuddin-east.name: Nizamuddin East
nizamuddin-east.about:
Nizamuddin East is a small and leafy residential colony on Mathura Road, with 286 houses and 32 public parks. Heritage monuments lie on its northern and southern edges, and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station is right next door, which also connects to the Pink Line. The colony sits inside the Ring Road, with Jangpura and Nizamuddin West nearby. Housing is almost entirely independent houses and floors.

Visits here are doorstep visits, usually with a guard or RWA check at the colony entrance, so let the gate know that a tutor is expected. The low-density layout makes parking easier than in most central colonies. Mathura Road and the station approach get busy in the evening, so tutors who drive may prefer a fixed slot outside the peak. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

nizamuddin-west.name: Nizamuddin West
nizamuddin-west.about:
Nizamuddin West is an upscale residential colony south of India Gate, surrounded by green spaces including Sunder Nursery, the Delhi Golf Club and Lodhi Gardens. It is also home to a historic dargah and the old basti around it, which draws visitors throughout the week. The residential blocks are made up of bungalows, independent houses and builder floors on tree-lined streets, and Khan Market is close by. Jangpura and Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium stations on the Violet Line are the nearest metro stations.

For tutors, the residential blocks are quiet and visits are straight to the door, often after checking in at an RWA gate. Roads near the dargah and basti get very crowded with visitors, so share the exact block and a gate landmark before the first visit. Tutors who drive should keep away from the basti lanes, and metro-based tutors can walk or take an auto from Jangpura. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini.name: Rohini
rohini.about:
Rohini is the large planned sub-city that the Delhi Development Authority began developing in the 1980s in North West Delhi, laid out as numbered sectors with pockets inside each. Housing is mostly DDA flats in LIG, MIG and HIG categories, cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies, and plotted pockets with builder floors and independent houses. The Red Line runs through the southern sectors to Rithala, the Yellow Line stops at Rohini Sector 18, 19 and Samaypur Badli, and since March 2026 the Magenta Line has stations at Deepali Chowk and Madhuban Chowk on the Outer Ring Road. Pitampura, Prashant Vihar and Shalimar Bagh lie alongside.

For home tuition, the sector and pocket number matter more than the name Rohini, because a tutor's route depends on which metro line is closest. CGHS societies usually register visitors at the gate, so share the tower and flat number in advance; DDA pockets and builder floors are generally a doorstep visit. Evening classes run more smoothly if the tutor's route avoids the Outer Ring Road rush. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-3.name: Rohini Sector 3
rohini-sector-3.about:
Sector 3 is one of the biggest sectors of Rohini and is split into lettered pockets from 3A to 3G, each with its own mix of DDA-allotted flats, builder floors and independent houses. It sits on the Outer Ring Road edge of the sub-city, beside Sector 8 and facing Pitampura. The Magenta Line station at Deepali Chowk, opened in March 2026, stands at the Sector 3/8 corner, and the Red Line stations formerly called Rohini West and Rohini East are the other rail options.

Because the sector is large, give the tutor your pocket letter as well as the house or flat number. Flats inside a society may need the tutor's name left at the gate, while builder floors and houses are usually a doorstep visit with street parking. A tutor coming by metro can get off at Deepali Chowk and finish by e-rickshaw; Outer Ring Road traffic builds in the evening, so a slightly earlier or later slot helps. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-5.name: Rohini Sector 5
rohini-sector-5.about:
At the western end of the Red Line, Sector 5 is home to Rithala metro station, which stands on Bhagwan Mahavir Marg inside the sector. Much of the housing here is builder floors, many of them larger three- and four-bedroom units, alongside the DDA-built stock that is common across Rohini. Bhagwan Mahavir Marg links the sector to the Outer Ring Road and to the other Rohini sectors, and the area has wide internal roads and plenty of green pockets.

Having the Red Line terminus inside the sector makes metro-based tutors practical: a short walk or e-rickshaw ride covers the last leg from Rithala. Builder floors are normally a doorstep visit, though a parent may need to buzz the tutor in at the ground-floor gate, and street parking suits tutors who drive. Families wanting a specialist subject that no nearby tutor covers can use online classes for that paper alone. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-7.name: Rohini Sector 7
rohini-sector-7.about:
Most homes in Sector 7 are DDA flats originally allotted to lower- and middle-income families, set among a mix of older blocks and newer construction. It lies in the older, southern part of Rohini next to Sectors 8 and 9, with Bhagwan Mahavir Marg and the Outer Ring Road as the main routes out. The nearest rail links are the two Red Line stations formerly known as Rohini West and Rohini East, both opened in March 2004.

DDA pockets are generally open to visitors, so a tutor usually walks straight to the block and flat; a clear block and flat number on the booking saves time. Parking inside the pockets can be tight in the evening, which is one reason many tutors here come by metro and e-rickshaw. Keeping sessions a little clear of the evening rush on the Outer Ring Road helps them start on time. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-8.name: Rohini Sector 8
rohini-sector-8.about:
Sector 8 is a mid-segment part of Rohini where the Delhi Development Authority built most of the housing, with HIG, MIG and LIG flats making up the bulk of homes. It is better connected by rail than most sectors: the Red Line station formerly called Rohini East (renamed Rohini in 2026) sits at the Sector 8/14 edge, Madhuban Chowk serves the sector on both the Red and Magenta Lines, and Deepali Chowk on the Magenta Line marks its corner with Sector 3. Pitampura lies across the Outer Ring Road, with Sectors 3, 9 and 14 around it.

With three stations close by, a tutor can nearly always reach Sector 8 by metro and a short walk or e-rickshaw ride. DDA blocks are usually a doorstep visit, but give the block and flat number clearly, as pocket layouts repeat. The chowks on the Outer Ring Road get busy in the evening, so tutors who drive should plan a buffer. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-9.name: Rohini Sector 9
rohini-sector-9.about:
Sector 9 is one of Rohini's more settled residential sectors, with housing dominated by DDA flats and RWA-managed cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies, plus a few private mid-rise complexes. Two- and three-bedroom flats are the typical home. It is surrounded by Sectors 7, 8, 10, 13, 14 and 15, and Bhagwan Mahavir Marg runs past it towards the Outer Ring Road. The Red Line station formerly called Rohini West is the nearest metro stop, with the old Rohini East station also within reach.

In CGHS societies the guard will usually ask for the tutor's name and flat number, so tell the gate in advance or add the tutor to the society's visitor list. DDA blocks are more open, and a tutor can go straight to the door. Metro plus e-rickshaw works well for tutors from other sectors, and a small gap before the evening peak on Bhagwan Mahavir Marg keeps timings steady. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-11.name: Rohini Sector 11
rohini-sector-11.about:
A quiet sector divided into several pockets, Sector 11 has a housing mix of DDA flats, builder floors and cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies, with a fair amount of green cover between the blocks. The sector has its own local shopping and banking, so daily errands rarely need a long trip. Rithala on the Red Line is usually the closest metro station, while Rohini Sector 18, 19 on the Yellow Line serves the northern side.

Before the first class, tell the tutor which pocket you live in, because the nearest station changes from one side of the sector to the other. Society flats may require a gate entry, whereas builder floors and DDA blocks are normally a doorstep visit. For board-exam years or specialist subjects, many Sector 11 families combine a home tutor for regular work with an online tutor for one paper. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-13.name: Rohini Sector 13
rohini-sector-13.about:
Low-rise flat complexes run by cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies make up much of Sector 13, alongside independent houses. It sits between Sectors 9, 14, 15 and 19, close to Prashant Vihar, Pitampura and Saraswati Vihar. Road access is via Bhagwan Mahavir Marg and the Outer Ring Road; for rail, residents use the Red Line stations formerly called Rohini West and Rohini East or the Yellow Line station at Rohini Sector 18, 19.

Most society gates keep a visitor register, so share the tutor's name with the guard or the RWA office before the demo class. Independent houses are a simple doorstep visit. Because the sector is between two metro lines, a tutor's travel is easiest to plan once you tell them which end of the sector you live on, and slots just before the evening peak on the Outer Ring Road tend to run on time. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-15.name: Rohini Sector 15
rohini-sector-15.about:
Sector 15 is a planned residential sector made up mainly of DDA flats in the LIG, MIG, HIG and Janta categories, with independent builder floors also in steady demand. Its closest metro is Rohini Sector 18, 19 on the Yellow Line, with Samaypur Badli and Haiderpur Badli Mor also nearby, while the Red Line station formerly called Rohini West serves its southern side. The Outer Ring Road and NH-44 provide the main road links.

DDA pockets are generally a doorstep visit; give the tutor the pocket, block and flat number together, since similar block names repeat across Rohini. Builder floors may need a parent to open the ground-floor gate. The Yellow Line makes it straightforward for tutors from North Campus and Model Town to reach Sector 15, and online classes are useful for subjects without a nearby tutor. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-16.name: Rohini Sector 16
rohini-sector-16.about:
Sector 16 is a densely built part of Rohini where most homes are in RWA-run societies or builder floors, with two- and three-bedroom units common. It sits between the Red and Yellow Line corridors: depending on the pocket, the nearest station is Rithala on the Red Line or Rohini Sector 18, 19 or Samaypur Badli on the Yellow Line. Local markets, eateries and everyday services are spread through the sector.

Because the nearest station varies by pocket, tell a tutor your exact pocket when you book so they can plan the metro leg and an e-rickshaw for the last stretch. Society gates usually record visitors, and builder floors are a doorstep visit with street parking that fills up in the evening. An earlier evening slot is often easier for tutors travelling across Rohini. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

rohini-sector-24.name: Rohini Sector 24
rohini-sector-24.about:
One of the outer sectors of Rohini, Sector 24 is organised into residential pockets, each with a gated feel, and much of the housing is DDA flats and MIG societies with private builder floors in between. The area also has local commercial centres and bank branches for everyday needs. Rithala on the Red Line is the usual rail link, with the rest of the journey by road.

Pocket gates in Sector 24 often have a guard, so the tutor's name and your flat number should be shared at the gate in advance. As the metro is not on the doorstep, tutors typically combine the Red Line with an e-rickshaw or come by two-wheeler, so fixed class timings help. Parking can be limited in the evening, and online classes are a practical option for specialist or senior-school subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

pitampura.name: Pitampura
pitampura.about:
Pitampura is a planned area of North West Delhi developed by the Delhi Development Authority in the 1980s. Housing includes DDA flats, among them large HIG towers, a string of enclaves with independent houses and builder floors, and apartment societies, while Netaji Subhash Place adds a busy commercial district. It is bordered by Rohini, Shalimar Bagh, Ashok Vihar and Model Town, and the Outer Ring Road runs along its edge. The Red Line stops at Madhuban Chowk (earlier called Pitampura), Kohat Enclave and Netaji Subhash Place, which is also on the Pink Line; the TV Tower and Dilli Haat Pitampura are well-known landmarks.
