With three stations inside the area, most tutors reach Pitampura by metro and a short e-rickshaw ride. Enclaves and builder floors are usually a doorstep visit, while DDA towers and societies may log visitors at the gate. Evening traffic around Netaji Subhash Place and the Outer Ring Road is heavy, so earlier slots suit tutors who drive. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

kohat-enclave.name: Kohat Enclave
kohat-enclave.about:
Kohat Enclave is a residential pocket of Pitampura made up mostly of independent houses and builder floors, many of them three- and four-bedroom homes, with small local markets in between. It is close to Netaji Subhash Place, Rohini and Shalimar Bagh, with Saraswati Vihar and Lok Vihar nearby, and the Outer Ring Road passes on one side. Its own Red Line station, Kohat Enclave, opened in March 2004.

Having a metro station inside the colony makes home tuition simple to arrange: a tutor can walk from the platform to most houses. Visits are usually straight to the door, though some lanes have an RWA gate with a guard who may ask where the tutor is going. Street parking fills up in the evenings, and traffic around Netaji Subhash Place builds at peak hour, so metro-travelling tutors tend to be the more punctual option. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

prashant-vihar.name: Prashant Vihar
prashant-vihar.about:
Prashant Vihar is a residential neighbourhood on the Outer Ring Road between Pitampura and the Rohini sectors, with Shalimar Bagh nearby. Homes are mainly builder floors and independent houses, along with some apartments and plots, and three-bedroom floors are the most common type. The area gained its own metro link in March 2026, when the Magenta Line station Uttari Pitampura-Prashant Vihar opened on the Outer Ring Road as part of the Deepali Chowk to Majlis Park stretch.

Most homes are independent floors, so a tutor usually comes straight to the door, and a parent may need to open the main gate for upper floors. The new Magenta Line station makes the area easier for tutors coming from Rohini, Pitampura or Majlis Park, with a short walk or e-rickshaw at the end. Outer Ring Road traffic is heaviest in the evening, so it helps to fix a slot that avoids the peak. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

shalimar-bagh.name: Shalimar Bagh
shalimar-bagh.about:
Shalimar Bagh is an established residential locality of North West Delhi laid out in lettered blocks. Its housing is mainly DDA flats and builder floors, with low-rise apartment blocks set around internal roads and parks; two- and three-bedroom homes form the bulk of the stock. The Outer Ring Road and GT Karnal Road carry most traffic, and Shalimar Bagh station on the Pink Line opened in March 2018. The locality takes its name from the Mughal-era Shalimar garden with its Sheesh Mahal, now protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Pitampura and Azadpur are neighbours.

Tell the tutor your block letter and house number, because blocks repeat similar numbering. DDA blocks and floors are normally a doorstep visit; low-rise apartment blocks may have a guard at the gate. The Pink Line plus an e-rickshaw is the easiest route for tutors from Pitampura or North Campus, and evening classes are easier to keep on time away from the Outer Ring Road peak. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

ashok-vihar.name: Ashok Vihar
ashok-vihar.about:
Built on land acquired from Wazirpur village, Ashok Vihar lies along the Ring Road in North West Delhi and is divided into four phases. Builder floors are the most common homes, with DDA flats, independent houses and a few apartment complexes making up the rest. Metro access comes from Keshav Puram and Kanhiya Nagar on the Red Line and Shalimar Bagh on the Pink Line, and Pitampura lies next door.

Since the four phases are spread out, share your phase and block as well as the house number when booking. Builder floors and houses are usually a doorstep visit, while DDA flats and complexes may note visitors at the gate. Tutors can use whichever station suits the phase and finish by e-rickshaw; Ring Road traffic is heavy at peak hours, so an early-evening slot is often easier. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

model-town.name: Model Town
model-town.about:
Model Town dates from the early 1950s and was one of Delhi's first privately developed neighbourhoods, planned with large plots and low-rise homes. It is divided into Model Town I, II and III, and today the housing is mostly three- and four-bedroom builder floors and independent houses. Naini Lake, with its boating and walking path, sits in the middle of Model Town I. The Yellow Line stops at Model Town and Azadpur, the latter also on the Pink Line, and the Ring Road and Outer Ring Road are both close. Neighbours include Azadpur, Kingsway Camp, Kamla Nagar and North Campus.

Most homes are independent floors, so tutors come straight to the door, though some blocks have RWA gates at night. The Yellow Line makes Model Town easy to reach from North Campus, Civil Lines and Rohini, with a short walk or e-rickshaw ride from the station. Street parking is tight in parts of Model Town I, so metro travel is often simpler for evening classes. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

adarsh-nagar.name: Adarsh Nagar
adarsh-nagar.about:
Adarsh Nagar is a residential and commercial neighbourhood of North West Delhi with bungalows, builder floors, DDA flats and independent homes, together with busy markets, wide roads and parks. It borders Azadpur, Shalimar Bagh, Jahangirpuri and Model Town. The Yellow Line station at Adarsh Nagar opened in February 2009, and Majlis Park, on the Pink and Magenta Lines, is close by.

Houses and builder floors are usually a doorstep visit, while DDA blocks may have an RWA gate. Tutors from Model Town, GTB Nagar or Rohini can come by the Yellow Line and walk or take an e-rickshaw from the station. Market streets get crowded in the evening and parking can be hard to find, so a tutor arriving by metro, or a class timed before the evening rush, tends to work better. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

gtb-nagar.name: GTB Nagar
gtb-nagar.about:
GTB Nagar is a mixed residential and student locality beside North Campus, and the older Kingsway Camp area forms part of it. Housing ranges from older residential buildings and apartments to hostels and paying-guest homes, with busy cafes around Hudson Lane. It borders Model Town, Mukherjee Nagar and Maurice Nagar, and NH-44 runs past it. The Yellow Line station at GTB Nagar, opened in February 2009, is in the heart of the area.

For a family here, the metro is the easiest way to bring in a tutor, since the station is within walking distance of most homes. Buildings are usually entered directly, though parking on side lanes is scarce. Traffic on Bhama Shah Marg is heavy at peak hours, so earlier evening slots are easier. Because the area is full of students, parents often find tutors living nearby for school subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mukherjee-nagar.name: Mukherjee Nagar
mukherjee-nagar.about:
Mukherjee Nagar is a North Delhi neighbourhood best known as a hub for civil-services exam preparation, with many coaching centres, libraries, bookshops and student hostels. The family housing is mostly DDA flats and builder floors, with two- and three-bedroom homes making up most of the stock. It lies next to North Campus, Hudson Lane, GTB Nagar, Kingsway Camp and Outram Lines, and GTB Nagar on the Yellow Line is the nearest metro station.

DDA blocks and builder floors are usually a doorstep visit, but main roads here are crowded with students and traffic in the evening, so give the tutor your block and the easiest lane to use. Many tutors come by the Yellow Line to GTB Nagar and finish by e-rickshaw. Families can pick from tutors living nearby for regular school subjects and add an online tutor for specialist papers. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

kamla-nagar.name: Kamla Nagar
kamla-nagar.about:
Kamla Nagar was built as a residential colony in the 1950s, laid out in six blocks with three roundabouts. It still has a mix of apartment buildings, bungalows and builder floors, but its market has grown into one of North Delhi's main shopping streets. Roop Nagar lies to the north, Shakti Nagar across the Grand Trunk Road to the west, and North Campus to the east. The nearest metro stations are Vishwavidyalaya on the Yellow Line and Pul Bangash on the Red Line.

Because the market draws crowds, especially in the evening, homes on the inner lanes are easier for a tutor to reach on foot from the metro than by car. Houses and floors are a doorstep visit; tell the tutor your block and the nearest roundabout. Parking near the market is very limited, so tutors who drive should allow extra time or pick an afternoon slot. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

civil-lines.name: Civil Lines
civil-lines.about:
Civil Lines is a colonial-era enclave laid out for British civilian officials, which now sits between the Yamuna and the northern Ridge. Spacious bungalows still make up most of the housing, with builder floors and apartments forming the rest, set among government buildings and tree-lined roads. Rajpur Road, Under Hill Road and the Ring Road run through it, the Yellow Line has a Civil Lines station, and Kashmere Gate interchange is close by. North Campus, Model Town, Mukherjee Nagar and Kingsway Camp are nearby.

Bungalows often have a guard or gatekeeper, so let them know the tutor's name before the first class. Parking is easier than in the denser colonies to the north, which suits tutors who drive, and metro users can come to Civil Lines station and walk or take an e-rickshaw. Evening traffic on the Ring Road can be heavy, so a class that starts before the rush is easier to keep on time. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mayur-vihar-phase-1.name: Mayur Vihar Phase 1
mayur-vihar-phase-1.about:
Mayur Vihar Phase 1 is one of the older planned parts of trans-Yamuna Delhi, developed by the DDA from the early 1980s. Housing is mostly DDA flats grouped into numbered pockets, in HIG, MIG and LIG categories, alongside cooperative group housing societies with their own gates. Pandav Nagar and Patparganj lie to the north and Trilokpuri to the east, while the DND Flyway and the Noida Link Road connect the area to South Delhi and Noida.

Mayur Vihar-I station is an interchange of the Blue and Pink lines, and the Pink Line also stops at Mayur Vihar Pocket 1 and Trilokpuri, so most homes have a station within easy reach. Many tutors arrive by metro and finish the last stretch on foot or by e-rickshaw. DDA pockets usually let a tutor walk straight to the flat, while society blocks keep a guard register and some like the tutor's name in advance. Evening slots are easier to keep if they avoid the office rush on the Noida Link Road. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mayur-vihar-phase-2.name: Mayur Vihar Phase 2
mayur-vihar-phase-2.about:
Set up in 1984, Mayur Vihar Phase 2 is a DDA colony whose flats are arranged in lettered pockets from A to F. It lies beside NH-9, the old NH-24 corridor that now carries the Delhi–Meerut Expressway, with Mayur Vihar Phase 1 on one side and East Vinod Nagar on its edge. The Noida Link Road is also close, which gives families quick road links to Noida, Ghaziabad and central Delhi.

East Vinod Nagar–Mayur Vihar-II station on the Pink Line, opened in October 2018, stands next to the colony, and the Blue Line at Mayur Vihar-I is also within reach. Tutors can usually walk or take an e-rickshaw from the station to the pocket. Some pockets have a gate with a guard, so sharing the pocket and flat number before the first class saves time at the entrance. The expressway and its service lanes get busy at office hours, so late-afternoon sessions that start before the evening rush tend to run on time. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mayur-vihar-phase-3.name: Mayur Vihar Phase 3
mayur-vihar-phase-3.about:
At the eastern end of the Mayur Vihar belt, close to the Noida border, Phase 3 has New Kondli and Gharoli beside it and Vasundhara Enclave next door. Housing is almost entirely DDA flats of several kinds: LIG pockets, MIG pockets, SFS pockets named A to D and Janta flats, along with a newer MIG complex built around 2005. It is a quieter, flat-based area rather than a market district.

The phase has no metro station of its own; the nearest are Mayur Vihar Extension and New Ashok Nagar on the Blue Line, and some residents use Noida Sector 15. A tutor coming by metro will normally need an auto or e-rickshaw for the last leg, so a little buffer time is sensible. Flats are reached through pocket gates rather than society reception desks, and evening parking inside the pockets can be tight, so a two-wheeler is often easier than a car. Online classes suit families who want a specialist subject teacher. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

patparganj.name: Patparganj
patparganj.about:
Patparganj is widely known for its cooperative group housing societies. Around 175 acres here were allotted to group housing societies, and multi-storey apartment blocks now make up much of the housing, along with some DDA flats and builder floors. The Patparganj industrial area lies close by, and Preet Vihar, Laxmi Nagar, Pandav Nagar and Mayur Vihar surround the locality, with NH-9 and the Noida Link Road as the main road links.

The nearest metro options are IP Extension and Mandawali–West Vinod Nagar on the Pink Line, with Preet Vihar on the Blue Line a little further. Almost every society has a staffed gate where visitors are logged, so tutors should expect to give their name and the flat number, and families can often pre-register a regular tutor with security. NH-9 and the Noida Link Road carry heavy office traffic, so early-evening slots are usually easier to keep than late ones. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

ip-extension.name: IP Extension
ip-extension.about:
IP Extension, short for Indraprastha Extension, is the society quarter of Patparganj: a planned cluster of mid-rise CGHS apartment complexes built on DDA-allotted land, with a few DDA blocks among them. Madhu Vihar, Mayur Vihar Phase 1, Preet Vihar, Hargobind Enclave and Anand Vihar are the neighbouring areas, and Vikas Marg and the Delhi–Meerut Expressway are the main roads out towards central Delhi and Ghaziabad.

IP Extension station on the Pink Line, opened in October 2018, serves the societies directly, while Preet Vihar on the Blue Line is an alternative. Because nearly every home is inside a gated complex, a tutor's first visit usually involves a gate entry and a call to the flat, so parents can save time by registering the tutor with security in advance. DTC buses along Vikas Marg help tutors without their own transport. For specialist subjects, online sessions widen the choice of teacher. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

pandav-nagar.name: Pandav Nagar
pandav-nagar.about:
Pandav Nagar is a well-established residential colony near the Akshardham temple, settled from around 1960. Today its housing is dominated by builder floors, with Ganesh Nagar forming part of the same complex, and Mayur Vihar Phase 1, Patparganj, IP Extension, Shakarpur and Laxmi Nagar all around it. The Delhi–Meerut Expressway passes by the colony, and the Noida Link Road is close at hand.

Akshardham on the Blue Line is the usual metro stop, with IP Extension on the Pink Line as another option. From either station an e-rickshaw brings a tutor to the lane, and since most homes are floors in independent buildings, the tutor goes straight to the family's door without a society gate. Lanes are narrow and parking is limited, so tutors on two-wheelers or public transport find visits simplest, and slots away from expressway rush hours are easier. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

vasundhara-enclave.name: Vasundhara Enclave
vasundhara-enclave.about:
Vasundhara Enclave is a compact Delhi enclave of about forty-four cooperative group housing societies, mostly low- to mid-rise apartment blocks along wide internal roads. It is bordered by Mayur Vihar to the north, Dallupura to the east, New Kondli to the south and New Ashok Nagar to the west, with Mayur Vihar Phase 3 alongside. It should not be confused with the Vasundhara township across the border.

New Ashok Nagar station on the Blue Line is the nearest metro, and the Namo Bharat station at New Ashok Nagar, opened in January 2025, now links the area to the Delhi–Meerut corridor. Tutors usually cover the last stretch by auto or cycle-rickshaw. Each society runs its own gate, so the first visit means a gate entry and a call to the flat; sharing the tutor's name with security beforehand keeps later visits quick. Online lessons are a practical option for advanced or specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

mandawali.name: Mandawali
mandawali.about:
Mandawali, often written Mandawali Fazalpur, grew from one of the oldest villages in East Delhi into a large colony that was regularised in 2012. Housing is mainly builder floors and independent houses in dense lanes, and the wider area takes in West Vinod Nagar, East Vinod Nagar and a busy local market. Patparganj, Preet Vihar, Laxmi Nagar, Shakarpur and IP Extension are its neighbours.

Mandawali–West Vinod Nagar station on the Pink Line, opened in 2018, is the main metro stop, and Karkarduma is also within reach. Patparganj Road and Shanti Marg carry most of the local traffic. A tutor visiting a builder floor goes straight to the door, but car parking in the inner lanes is hard to find, so metro plus e-rickshaw or a two-wheeler is the practical way in. The main roads are busiest in the evening market hours, so many families prefer an earlier slot. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

shakarpur.name: Shakarpur
shakarpur.about:
Shakarpur sits between Laxmi Nagar and Mayur Vihar and is one of the busier older colonies of East Delhi. Most homes are builder floors and independent houses, with some multi-storey apartments, and the colony has plenty of shops and wholesale markets. Pandav Nagar, Ganesh Nagar, West Vinod Nagar and Laxmi Nagar border it, and Vikas Marg, Patparganj Road and the Noida Link Road are the main roads.

Laxmi Nagar station on the Blue Line is the closest metro, with Nirman Vihar and Akshardham as alternatives. Because housing is in individual buildings, tutors go straight to the family's floor, though they may need to ring from the street door. Lanes are narrow and parking is scarce, so metro with an e-rickshaw or a two-wheeler is the usual approach. Vikas Marg is heavily used at office hours, so afternoon sessions before the evening peak are easier to hold. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

laxmi-nagar.name: Laxmi Nagar
laxmi-nagar.about:
Laxmi Nagar is the busiest hub of trans-Yamuna Delhi, known across the city for its many chartered accountancy, cost accounting and company secretary coaching centres, and for garment and daily-needs shopping. Homes are mostly builder floors and some apartments in lanes off Vikas Marg, and the area blends into Shakarpur, Preet Vihar, Nirman Vihar, Patparganj, Geeta Colony and Lalita Park.

Laxmi Nagar station on the Blue Line, part of the branch opened in January 2010, sits within the locality, with Nirman Vihar and Akshardham nearby. The inner lanes are narrow and parking is scarce, so tutors mostly come by metro and walk or take an e-rickshaw. Families in builder floors let the tutor straight in, with no society gate to pass. Vikas Marg slows sharply at peak hours, so booking lessons outside the office rush saves travel, and online classes are useful for specialist subjects. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

preet-vihar.name: Preet Vihar
preet-vihar.about:
Preet Vihar is a well-regarded plotted colony of East Delhi and gives its name to one of the district's administrative subdivisions. Housing is mainly independent houses and builder floors laid out in lettered blocks, with Madhuban Enclave and Nirman Vihar next door and Laxmi Nagar, Mandawali, Swasthya Vihar, Madhu Vihar and Anand Vihar close by.

Vikas Marg is the main road, and Preet Vihar station on the Blue Line, opened in January 2010, sits on it; Karkarduma Court on the Pink Line is another option. Some blocks have RWA gates with a guard who notes visitors, so the tutor's name should be shared before the first day, after which visits go straight to the house. Patparganj Road is the other key link to the south. Vikas Marg traffic builds up in the rush hours, so late-afternoon slots usually work better than evening ones for regular lessons. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

nirman-vihar.name: Nirman Vihar
nirman-vihar.about:
Nirman Vihar is a small, low-rise colony on Vikas Marg, made up largely of independent builder floors. It sits beside Preet Vihar and Laxmi Nagar, with Shakarpur and Chitra Vihar close by, and its position on the main road gives easy access towards Connaught Place in one direction and Noida in the other. It is a quiet residential pocket despite the busy road outside.

Nirman Vihar station on the Blue Line, opened in January 2010, serves the colony directly, so tutors travelling by metro can usually walk to the house. Visits are straightforward because homes are separate buildings, though some lanes may have an RWA gate where the guard notes visitors. Vikas Marg carries heavy traffic at peak hours, so parents often choose slots before the evening rush, and tutors on two-wheelers find parking simpler than those in cars. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

karkardooma.name: Karkardooma
karkardooma.about:
Karkardooma mixes cooperative group housing societies and apartments with some independent houses, close to the Karkarduma Court metro station. Anand Vihar, Surajmal Vihar, Krishna Nagar, Madhu Vihar and Swasthya Vihar are the neighbours, and Vikas Marg and NH-9 are the main road links. The DDA is also building a large transit-oriented housing hub beside the metro interchange.

Karkarduma station is an interchange of the Blue Line, opened in 2010, and the Pink Line, whose platform is among the highest in the network. With many families living in gated societies, tutors should expect a gate entry and a call to the flat on the first visit, and parents can save time by giving security the tutor's name. Vikas Marg and the approaches to Anand Vihar are busiest at office hours, so lessons timed before the evening rush run more smoothly. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

anand-vihar.name: Anand Vihar
anand-vihar.about:
The residential part of Anand Vihar is a colony of builder floors, independent houses and some apartments set around one of Delhi's biggest transport hubs: the Anand Vihar railway terminal, the interstate bus terminal and a Namo Bharat station. Karkardooma, Preet Vihar, Surajmal Vihar, IP Extension and Krishna Nagar are the neighbouring areas, and Vikas Marg and NH-9 are the main roads.

Anand Vihar metro station serves both the Blue and Pink lines, and the underground Namo Bharat station, opened in January 2025, links to the Delhi–Meerut corridor. Tutors can reach the colony easily by metro, then walk or take an e-rickshaw to the house. Since homes are mostly independent buildings, visits go straight to the door, though some lanes have RWA gates. Traffic around the terminals is heavy for much of the day, so tutors arriving by road should allow a buffer, especially at peak hours. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

vivek-vihar.name: Vivek Vihar
vivek-vihar.about:
Vivek Vihar is a low-rise, plotted colony near the Delhi–Uttar Pradesh border, divided into Phase 1 and Phase 2 with blocks A to D. Builder floors and independent houses make up most of the housing, and residents often point out that its roads are wider than in many East Delhi colonies. Jhilmil Colony, Surajmal Vihar, Vishwas Nagar, Anand Vihar and Dilshad Garden are all close by.

GT Road is the main road nearby, and metro users rely on Dilshad Garden and Jhilmil on the Red Line, with Anand Vihar and Karkarduma on the Blue and Pink lines a little further off. Tutors usually cover the last stretch by e-rickshaw. Houses are reached directly, though several blocks have RWA gates where the guard notes visitors, so sharing the tutor's name early helps. Main-road traffic peaks in the evening, so earlier slots are easier to keep. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

surajmal-vihar.name: Surajmal Vihar
surajmal-vihar.about:
Surajmal Vihar is a planned plotted colony in East Delhi where builder floors, independent houses and residential plots make up the housing, and three-bedroom homes are the most common. It lies close to Karkardooma and Vivek Vihar, with Ram Vihar, Vishwas Nagar, Hargobind Enclave and Jagriti Enclave as its immediate neighbours, and it is a largely residential, low-rise area.

Karkarduma station, an interchange of the Blue and Pink lines, is the nearest metro, and Anand Vihar is also close, so tutors often come by metro and take an e-rickshaw for the last part. Some blocks have RWA-managed gates, so families should share the tutor's name with the guard before the first lesson; after that the tutor goes straight to the house. Main roads around Karkardooma and Anand Vihar are busy in the evening, so late-afternoon slots tend to be easier. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

krishna-nagar.name: Krishna Nagar
krishna-nagar.about:
Krishna Nagar is a long-established, mid-budget residential ward of East Delhi with lettered blocks A to K and neighbouring pockets such as East Krishna Nagar, Jagatpuri and Ram Nagar. Housing is a mix of independent houses, builder floors and some apartments, and the busy Lal Quarter market is the local shopping hub. It sits near Gandhi Nagar, Geeta Colony, Preet Vihar and Vishwas Nagar, with Patparganj Road along its western side.

Krishna Nagar station on the Pink Line, opened in 2018, serves the colony, with Karkarduma on the Blue and Pink lines close by. Internal roads are narrow and parking is under pressure, so tutors usually rely on the metro and a walk or e-rickshaw, or a two-wheeler. Homes are separate buildings, so tutors go straight to the door. The market area is crowded in the evening, so lessons earlier in the afternoon or on weekend mornings are easier to keep. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

geeta-colony.name: Geeta Colony
geeta-colony.about:
Geeta Colony is an older, closely built residential colony of East Delhi, bordered by Gandhi Nagar, Laxmi Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Kundan Nagar and Krishan Kunj. Some lanes still have older independent homes, while many plots have been rebuilt as builder floors with parking and lifts. Neighbourhood markets, parks and everyday services are spread through and around the colony.

Metro access comes from several directions: Nirman Vihar, Laxmi Nagar and Preet Vihar on the Blue Line, East Azad Nagar on the Pink Line and Seelampur on the Red Line. Tutors usually finish the journey by e-rickshaw, and visits go straight to the family's floor. The colony is crowded and parking is hard to find, so public transport or a two-wheeler is the practical choice. Main roads are heavy at peak hours, so slots outside the rush suit tutors better. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

shahdara.name: Shahdara
shahdara.about:
Shahdara is one of the oldest inhabited parts of Delhi, a grain-trading centre in the eighteenth century that now gives its name to a whole district formed in 2012. The locality mixes residential colonies for middle- and upper-middle-class families with busy commercial streets, and it links naturally to Dilshad Garden, Anand Vihar and Gandhi Nagar. GT Road and Loni Road are the main roads, and Delhi Shahdara Junction is a major railway station.

Shahdara station on the Red Line opened in December 2002 as part of Delhi Metro's very first section, and Welcome station, where the Red and Pink lines meet, is close by. Tutors can use the metro and then an e-rickshaw through the lanes. Lanes are congested and parking is tight, so two-wheelers or public transport work better than cars, and GT Road is busiest at office hours, so earlier or weekend slots are easier. Online classes help families looking for specialist teachers. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

dilshad-garden.name: Dilshad Garden
dilshad-garden.about:
Dilshad Garden is a large DDA colony developed in the late 1970s and early 1980s, organised into blocks and pockets, each with its own market and parks. Most families live in DDA flats, with GTB Enclave and Dilshad Colony forming part of the wider area, and Jhilmil Colony, Vivek Vihar, Shahdara and Mansarovar Park close by. GT Road runs past the colony towards the Uttar Pradesh border.

Dilshad Garden and Jhilmil stations on the Red Line, both opened in June 2008, serve the colony and connect it towards Shahdara and the rest of the network. Tutors can walk or take an e-rickshaw from the station into the pockets. Some pockets have gates with a guard, so sharing the block and flat number in advance helps. GT Road is busiest at office hours, so lessons timed before the evening peak are easier to keep for both tutor and child. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

yamuna-vihar.name: Yamuna Vihar
yamuna-vihar.about:
Yamuna Vihar is a planned residential area of North East Delhi made up of blocks B-1 to B-5 and C-1 to C-12, with Bhajanpura often described locally as its A block. Housing is mainly DDA-plotted builder floors and small independent plots, giving mostly low-rise streets. Shahdara, Maujpur and Bhajanpura are its neighbours, and Wazirabad Road is the main route, crossing the Yamuna over the Signature Bridge.

The Pink Line now has a Yamuna Vihar station on the stretch that completed the ring in March 2026, and Maujpur–Babarpur on the Pink Line and Shastri Park and Seelampur on the Red Line are other options. Tutors go straight to the house, as these are separate buildings, though some blocks have RWA gates where visitors are noted. Parking near the main road is scarce, so a two-wheeler or metro plus e-rickshaw is the easier choice, and Wazirabad Road is heavy at peak hours, so earlier slots help. Home tutors from nearby sectors and online tutors are available on NXTutors, with a free demo class.

GK, Defence Colony & Lajpat Nagar.fact: Lajpat Nagar metro station is an interchange: the Violet Line platforms opened on 3 October 2010 and the Pink Line platforms on 6 August 2018.
The Violet Line's first section, Central Secretariat to Sarita Vihar, opened on 3 October 2010 and runs through Jangpura, Lajpat Nagar, Moolchand, Kailash Colony and Nehru Place.
The Pink Line section through South Extension and Lajpat Nagar opened on 6 August 2018.
Greater Kailash metro station on the Magenta Line opened on 29 May 2018.
Greater Kailash was developed from the early 1960s on agricultural land from Zamrudpur and Devli villages acquired by the government in 1955.
Defence Colony was established in 1960 to resettle military officers displaced by Partition, on land formerly of Kotla Mubarakpur village.
Lajpat Nagar I, II and III lie north of the Ring Road, and Lajpat Nagar IV lies south of it.

Saket, Malviya Nagar & Hauz Khas.fact: The Yellow Line section from Qutab Minar to Central Secretariat opened on 3 September 2010, with stations at Green Park, Hauz Khas, Malviya Nagar and Saket.
Hauz Khas station is an interchange: Yellow Line from 3 September 2010 and Magenta Line from 29 May 2018; it is the deepest station in the Delhi Metro network.
The Magenta Line section from Kalkaji Mandir to Janakpuri West, including Panchsheel Park and Chirag Delhi, opened in May 2018.
Chhatarpur station on the Yellow Line opened on 26 August 2010 and is the only Delhi Metro station built entirely of steel.
Saket was developed by the DDA on land of the Khirki, Said-ul-Ajaib and Hauz Rani villages.
The Outer Ring Road passes the IIT/Hauz Khas and Chirag Delhi junctions and runs past Panchsheel Park.

Kalkaji, CR Park & Sarita Vihar.fact: Kalkaji Mandir station is an interchange: Violet Line from 3 October 2010 and Magenta Line from 25 December 2017.
The first Magenta Line section, Botanical Garden to Kalkaji Mandir, opened on 25 December 2017.
Jasola Vihar Shaheen Bagh station on the Magenta Line opened on 25 December 2017.
Sarita Vihar station, in Pocket C of the colony, opened with the first Violet Line section on 3 October 2010.
Sarita Vihar was built on land of Madanpur Khadar village and was first planned for the 1982 Asian Games.
Chittaranjan Park was set up in the early 1960s as the East Pakistan Displaced Persons (EPDP) Colony and renamed in the 1980s.
The Violet Line was extended from Sarita Vihar to Badarpur Border on 14 January 2011.
The Outer Ring Road has a flyover junction at Kalkaji/Nehru Place and another at Modi Mill.

Dwarka.fact: Dwarka is a sub-city developed by the Delhi Development Authority, organised into sectors, with cooperative group housing societies as the main residential option; its area is 5,648 hectares as per DDA records.
The Blue Line section from Barakhamba Road to Dwarka opened on 31 December 2005.
The Blue Line was extended from Dwarka to Dwarka Sector 9 on 1 April 2006, and from Dwarka Sector 9 to Dwarka Sector 21 on 30 October 2010.
Blue Line stations in Dwarka include Dwarka Sector 21, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14, Dwarka and Dwarka Mor.
Dwarka Sector 21 is an interchange between the Blue Line and the Airport Express Line, which opened on 23 February 2011.
Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector 25 station opened on 17 September 2023, extending the Airport Express Line westwards to the India International Convention and Expo Centre.

The Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB) starts from NH-48 at Shiv Murti near Mahipalpur; its Delhi section passes Dwarka Sectors 21, 22, 25, 27 and 28 before entering Haryana, where most of its length lies. The full route became operational in June 2025.

Vasant Kunj, Vasant Vihar & Palam.fact: The Magenta Line section from Janakpuri West to Botanical Garden opened on 29 May 2018, with stations including Dabri Mor - Janakpuri South, Dashrathpuri, Palam, Vasant Vihar, Munirka and R K Puram.
Nelson Mandela Marg runs through Vasant Kunj, which is divided into lettered sectors subdivided into pockets and blocks.
Vasant Vihar has six blocks (A to F); its main streets are Munirka Marg, Vasant Marg, Poorvi Marg and Paschimi Marg, and it houses more than 50 diplomatic missions.
The notification for the urbanisation of Munirka was issued in March 1954.
R K Puram was developed by the Central Public Works Department from the late 1950s as an extension of New Delhi, mainly with housing for central government officers.
Palam lies between Delhi Cantonment, Dwarka and Janakpuri; Palam railway station connects to Rewari, Delhi Cantonment and New Delhi.
The Sultan Ghari tomb, described as the first Islamic mausoleum in Delhi, is in the Vasant Kunj area.

Janakpuri, Rajouri Garden & Punjabi Bagh.fact: The Blue Line section from Barakhamba Road to Dwarka, which includes the stations along Najafgarh Road such as Rajouri Garden, Subhash Nagar, Tilak Nagar and Janakpuri, opened on 31 December 2005.
Janakpuri West became an interchange between the Blue Line (open since 31 December 2005) and the Magenta Line, which reached it on 29 May 2018.
The Green Line opened from Inderlok to Mundka on 3 April 2010, serving Punjabi Bagh and Paschim Vihar, and its Kirti Nagar to Ashok Park Main branch opened on 27 August 2011.
Punjabi Bagh West station opened on 29 March 2022 as an interchange between the Green Line and the Pink Line.
The Pink Line's first section, from Majlis Park to Durgabai Deshmukh South Campus, opened on 14 March 2018; Naraina Vihar station opened that day.
Janakpuri was planned in the late 1960s as the largest residential colony in Asia.

Punjabi Bagh was built on land acquired from Madipur village to resettle refugees from Pakistan; it was called Refugees Colony until it was renamed in 1960, and the Ring Road divides it into East and West.
Moti Nagar was formed in 1948 to 1950 with help from the Delhi Improvement Trust as a resettlement colony.

Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar & Rajinder Nagar.fact: Karol Bagh, Rajendra Place, Patel Nagar and Shadipur stations are on the Blue Line section from Barakhamba Road to Dwarka, which opened on 31 December 2005.
Karol Bagh received villagers displaced by the building of Connaught Place in the 1920s, and after Partition in 1947 took in many refugees from West Punjab and Sindh.
Rajinder Nagar developed in the 1950s as a Punjabi refugee colony, and Shankar Road divides it into Old and New Rajinder Nagar.
Rajinder Nagar is one of Delhi's two main education hubs for government job aspirants, known especially for civil services coaching.

Patel Nagar was developed on land acquired from Shadipur, Khampur and neighbouring villages and is divided into East, West and South Patel Nagar, served by Rajendra Place, Patel Nagar and Shadipur stations.
Karol Bagh's main markets include Ajmal Khan Road, Ghaffar Market, Arya Samaj Road and Bank Street.

Lodhi Colony, Jangpura & Nizamuddin.fact: The Violet Line section from Central Secretariat to Sarita Vihar, including Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and Jangpura stations, opened on 3 October 2010.
Lodhi Colony was built in the 1940s to house government employees and is governed by the New Delhi Municipal Council.
Lodhi Colony is described as India's first open-air public art district, after artists painted murals across the colony.
Jangpura grew in 1950 to 1951 with the arrival of many Sikh and Hindu migrants from the Punjab province of Pakistan.
Nizamuddin East has 286 houses and 32 public parks and lies on Mathura Road.
The Pink Line was extended from Lajpat Nagar to Shree Ram Mandir Mayur Vihar on 31 December 2018, bringing it to Hazrat Nizamuddin.

Rohini.fact: Rohini was developed as a sub-city project of the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), started in the 1980s to house a mix of income groups.
The Red Line was extended from Inderlok to Rithala on 31 March 2004; Rithala, the stations formerly called Rohini West and Rohini East, and Pitampura (now Madhuban Chowk) opened then.
The Red Line station at the Sector 8/14 edge, formerly Rohini East, was renamed Rohini; the change was approved by Delhi's State Names Authority in May 2026.
Rohini Sector 18, 19, Samaypur Badli and Haiderpur Badli Mor stations on the Yellow Line opened on 10 November 2015.
The Magenta Line stretch from Deepali Chowk to Majlis Park (seven stations) opened on 8 March 2026.
Deepali Chowk metro station stands on the Outer Ring Road at the Sector 3/8 corner of Rohini, beside Pitampura.
Madhuban Chowk station, on the Outer Ring Road serving Sector 8 Rohini and Pitampura, was earlier called Pitampura and is an interchange between the Red and Magenta Lines.

Pitampura, Model Town & North Campus.fact: Vishwavidyalaya, Vidhan Sabha and Civil Lines stations opened on 20 December 2004 in the first Yellow Line section.
GTB Nagar, Model Town, Azadpur, Adarsh Nagar and Jahangirpuri stations on the Yellow Line opened on 4 February 2009.
On the Pink Line, Majlis Park, Azadpur, Shalimar Bagh and Netaji Subhash Place stations opened on 14 March 2018.
Kohat Enclave, Netaji Subhash Place and Keshav Puram stations on the Red Line opened on 31 March 2004.
Uttari Pitampura-Prashant Vihar station on the Outer Ring Road opened on 8 March 2026 as part of the Magenta Line's Deepali Chowk to Majlis Park stretch.
Pitampura was developed by the DDA in the 1980s; its TV Tower dates from 1988 and Dilli Haat Pitampura opened in April 2008.
Model Town was built in the early 1950s as one of Delhi's first privately developed neighbourhoods and is divided into Model Town I, II and III, with Naini Lake in Model Town I.

Mayur Vihar, Patparganj & IP Extension.fact: Mayur Vihar-I, Mayur Vihar Extension and New Ashok Nagar stations on the Blue Line opened on 12 November 2009 with the Yamuna Bank – Noida City Centre section.
The Pink Line section from Trilokpuri – Sanjay Lake to Shiv Vihar, including East Vinod Nagar – Mayur Vihar-II, Mandawali – West Vinod Nagar and IP Extension stations, opened on 31 October 2018.
The Pink Line gap between Mayur Vihar Pocket-1 and Trilokpuri – Sanjay Lake, delayed by land acquisition, was bridged on 6 August 2021, making the line a single corridor.
The DND Flyway opened on 24 January 2001, linking Maharani Bagh and Nizamuddin with Noida and Mayur Vihar across the Yamuna; a Mayur Vihar link opened in 2008.
Phase I of the Delhi–Meerut Expressway, a 14-lane stretch from Nizamuddin Bridge to the UP border along NH-9 (old NH-24), was inaugurated on 27 May 2018.
In Patparganj, 175 acres of land were allocated to various group housing societies.
Mayur Vihar Phase II was set up in 1984 with DDA flats in pockets A to F; Phase III is made up of DDA LIG, MIG, SFS and Janta flats.
Vasundhara Enclave (Delhi) has about forty-four group housing societies and adjoins Dallupura, Mayur Vihar, New Kondli and New Ashok Nagar.

Laxmi Nagar, Preet Vihar & Shahdara.fact: The Blue Line branch stations Laxmi Nagar, Nirman Vihar, Preet Vihar, Karkarduma and Anand Vihar opened on 6 January 2010.
Shahdara, Welcome, Seelampur and Shastri Park stations opened on 25 December 2002 with the Tis Hazari – Shahdara section, the first section of the Delhi Metro.
The Red Line was extended to Mansarovar Park, Jhilmil and Dilshad Garden on 4 June 2008.

Karkarduma is an interchange of the Blue Line (opened 6 January 2010) and the Pink Line (opened 31 October 2018); its Pink Line platform, about 20 m above ground, is the second highest in the Delhi Metro network.

The Anand Vihar Namo Bharat (RRTS) station opened on 5 January 2025 and is the only underground station on the Delhi–Meerut corridor, with interchanges to the Blue and Pink lines, Anand Vihar Terminal and the interstate bus terminal.
The Pink Line became a complete ring on 8 March 2026, with the Majlis Park – Maujpur stretch that includes Yamuna Vihar station.
Shahdara district was formed in September 2012, with Shahdara, Vivek Vihar and Seemapuri subdivisions.
Dilshad Garden was developed by the DDA in the late 1970s and early 1980s, mostly as DDA flats in blocks and pockets.
